compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
## Problem

A run that repairs CI more than once records the wrong repair usage. The stored row reports only the final attempt, so an operator reading usage metrics sees a fraction of what the run spent, and the figure disagrees with the budget accounting that parked the run.

`record_usage_metrics` writes one row per `(execution_id, stage)` pair and overwrites it on every write. `DraftPullRequestWorkflow._repair` writes `stage="REPAIRING"` once per attempt with that attempt's own numbers, so attempt three overwrites attempt two, which overwrote attempt one. Three attempts costing 0.1 each leave 0.1 on record rather than 0.3.

Two further defects sit in the same lines.

`cache_read_tokens` is never passed to `UsageMetrics`, so the column stores zero for every repair however much the model read from cache. The field is carried on `ApplyCIRepairResult` and accumulated into `self._repair_cache_read_tokens`, then dropped at the write.

Accumulation happens in the caller rather than in `_repair`. The `run` loop adds the four counters to their running totals after `_repair` returns, which is after `_repair` has already written the usage row. The stored row is therefore always one attempt behind the budget state that `_budget_breach` reads, so the two can never agree even once the total is written.

## Cause

The usage write treats a stage row as an append when the store treats it as an upsert. Per-attempt values are correct for a log and wrong for a row that survives only in its last form. The accumulation sits on the wrong side of the activity call, and one of the four accumulated counters is never forwarded.

## Approach

Write the running total, and accumulate before the write rather than after it.

- Move the four `self._repair_*` accumulations out of the `run` loop and into `_repair`, placed immediately after the `apply_ci_repair` activity returns and before the `record_usage_metrics` call. The loop no longer needs them because `_repair` owns them.
- Pass `self._repair_tokens`, `self._repair_cost` and `self._repair_llm_calls` to `UsageMetrics` in place of the per-attempt `repair.tokens`, `repair.cost` and `repair.llm_calls`.
- Pass `cache_read_tokens=self._repair_cache_read_tokens`, which the write omitted entirely.

Ordering is what makes the row agree with the budget. `_budget_breach` reads the same `self._repair_*` fields, so once the accumulation precedes the write, the surviving row equals the figure that decides whether the run parks.

A single repair attempt is unaffected, because a running total over one attempt is that attempt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Successive `REPAIRING` usage records carry the running cost rather than the per-attempt cost, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k running_total`
- [x] The `REPAIRING` usage record carries a non-zero `cache_read_tokens` when the repair activity reports one, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k running_total`
- [x] The cumulative budget test asserts the rising cost sequence rather than a constant per-attempt cost, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py -k cumulative_budget`
- [x] The full workflow unit suite passes, checked by `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py`

## Testing

A new workflow test drives three repair attempts under a cost budget that parks the run, then reads the `REPAIRING` usage records the activity captured. It asserts the cost sequence rises as 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 rather than repeating 0.1, and that `cache_read_tokens` carries the value the repair activity returned. The existing cumulative budget test asserted a constant per-attempt cost, which encoded the defect, so it is updated to assert the same rising sequence.

`_make_activities` gains a `repair_cache_read_tokens` argument so a test can make the repair activity report cache reads, which previously defaulted to zero and hid the dropped field.

Commands:

- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_draft_pull_request_workflow.py`
- `.venv/bin/ruff check services tests`

file_impact.reason: Move the four repair counter accumulations into _repair before the usage write, and pass the running totals plus cache_read_tokens to UsageMetrics

Add a test proving successive repair records carry the running total and the cache read tokens, add repair_cache_read_tokens to _make_activities, and correct the cumulative budget assertion that encoded the per-attempt cost
